For a [[cryptographic hash function]] (a mathematical [[algorithm]]), a '''MASH-1''' ('''Modular Arithmetic Secure Hash''') is a [[hash function]] based on [[modular arithmetic]].

== History ==
Despite many proposals, few hash functions based on modular arithmetic have withstood attack, and most that have tend to be relatively inefficient.  MASH-1 evolved from a long line of related proposals successively broken and repaired.

== Standard ==
Committee Draft ISO/IEC 10118-4 (Nov 95)

== Description ==
MASH-1 involves use of an [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]]-like modulus <math>N</math>, whose bitlength affects the security. <math>N</math> is a product of two [[prime number]]s and should be difficult to [[factorization|factor]], and for <math>N</math> of unknown factorization, the security is based in part on the difficulty of extracting modular roots.

Let <math>L</math> be the length of a message block in [[bit]]. <math>N</math> is chosen to have a binary representation a few bits longer than <math>L</math>, typically <math>L < |N| \leq L+16</math>.

The message is padded by appending the message length and is separated into blocks <math>D_1, \cdots, D_q</math> of length <math>L/2</math>. From each of these blocks <math>D_i</math>, an enlarged block <math>B_i</math> of length <math>L</math> is created by placing four bits from <math>D_i</math> in the lower half of each byte and four bits of value 1 in the higher half. These blocks are processed iteratively by a compression function:

:<math>H_0 = IV</math>
:<math>H_i = f(B_i, H_{i-1}) = ((((B_i \oplus H_{i-1}) \vee E)^e \bmod N) \bmod 2^L) \oplus H_{i-1}; \quad i=1,\cdots,q</math>

Where <math>E=15 \cdot 2^{L-4}</math> and <math>e=2</math>. <math>\vee</math> denotes the [[Bitwise operation#OR|bitwise OR]] and <math>\oplus</math> the [[Bitwise operation#XOR|bitwise XOR]].

From <math>H_q</math> are now calculated more data blocks <math>D_{q+1},\cdots,D_{q+8}</math> by linear operations (where <math>\|</math> denotes concatenation):

:<math>H_q = Y_1 \,\|\, Y_3 \,\|\, Y_0 \,\|\, Y_2; \quad |Y_i| = L/4</math>
:<math>Y_i = Y_{i-1} \oplus Y_{i-4}; \quad i=4,\cdots,15</math>
:<math>D_{q+i} = Y_{2i-2} \,\|\, Y_{2i-1}; \quad i=1,\cdots,8</math>

These data blocks are now enlarged to <math>B_{q+1},\cdots,B_{q+8}</math> like above, and with these the compression process continues with eight more steps:
:<math>H_i = f(B_i, H_{i-1}); \quad i=q+1,\cdots,q+8</math>

Finally the hash value is <math>H_{q+8} \bmod p</math>, where <math>p</math> is a prime number with <math>7\cdot 2^{L/2-3} < p < 2^{L/2}</math>.<ref>[https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/589.pdf Smashing MASH-1, Vladimir Antipkin]</ref>

== MASH-2 ==
There is a newer version of the algorithm called MASH-2 with a different exponent. The original <math>e=2</math> is replaced by <math>e=2^8+1</math>. This is the only difference between these versions.
